title: Lunch service: 20 meals
narration: Stage One gives us checked four- and eight-hour schedules. Our extension schedules catering batches: both courses must reach the same departure, and unused food counts as waste.

title: Two orders sharing a side batch
narration: Two customers each need ten meals. Main A is already cooking. We choose Main B and a twenty-portion side batch shared between both orders. The schedule assigns equipment, workers, preparation, cooking, packing and cleaning. Separate cookers can overlap, but both orders use the same packing line.

live_narration: Each customer needs ten meals. Main A is already cooking. We choose a new Main B and one shared side batch. Preparation, cooking, packing and cleaning reserve real equipment and workers. Both orders share the packing line.

title: What happens without the side batch
narration: Remove the side batch and neither order receives a complete meal, despite both mains being cooked. Twenty component portions are discarded. This is a checked manual intervention that exposes the consequence of a batch choice.
live_narration: Remove the side batch and we serve no complete meals. Twenty component portions become waste. This is a checked manual intervention.

title: Batch selection and scheduling constraints
narration: Each program describes one batch: quantity, allocations, equipment, crew and phase times. A bit selects it. Programs sharing an anchor demand form a one-hot block with an idle choice. Cross-block penalties forbid duplicate allocations and resource clashes. The small cell includes all thirty-two legal programs, plus three idle bits.
live_action: Play past halfway for the compiler excerpt.
live_narration: A bit selects one batch program: quantity, allocations, resources and times. One-hot blocks choose a program or idle; pairwise penalties forbid clashes. The small cell offers all thirty-two legal programs, plus three idle bits.

title: Complete meals and food waste
narration: For a meal lot, binary main coverage times side coverage gives complete service. Their sum minus twice their product counts unpaired components. Coverage is linear in batch-selection bits, so both expressions remain quadratic without auxiliary product bits. We prioritize missed meals, waste, batches and plan changes. Integer bounds prove that ordering and the hard-constraint penalty.
live_action: Point to MS, then the priority order.
live_narration: Main coverage times side coverage gives complete service. Their sum minus twice the product counts unpaired food. Both expand quadratically without product bits. We prove the objective priority order and a penalty bound that makes every ground state feasible.

title: Mandatory cleaning after repair
narration: A repaired cooker still needs cleaning. Here the qualified worker first finishes committed work, then cleans the repaired cooker from eleven forty to eleven fifty. Both worker and cooker are reserved. The independent checker reconstructs these intervals, freshness and meal handovers from raw schedule records.

title: Local QAOA sampling
narration: QAOA applies cost and conflict phases followed by blockwise XY mixing. We now sample the saved angles locally, without retraining. The mixer preserves one choice per block; equipment, worker and allocation conflicts still need checking. Every distinct returned bitstring is decoded and checked. The receipt reports complete meals, waste and valid shots.
live_narration: QAOA uses cost phases and blockwise XY mixing. The mixer preserves one choice per block, while the checker still rejects cross-block conflicts. This button samples saved angles locally and checks the returned schedules.

title: Results against exact and classical references
narration: All six small-cell trials find the certified optimum; the controls find it too. On the larger pilot, six of eight final plans match their final offered-pool optimum. All eight trail the full-grid reference, and final-step controls tie. A solver cannot recover a good schedule excluded by its representation: we measure that loss separately from search.
live_action: Show the cell outcome and larger comparison.
live_narration: Six cell trials find the optimum, as do the controls. Six of eight larger final plans attain their offered-pool optimum, but all trail the full grid. We distinguish missing choices from poor search; neither is hidden by a success headline.

title: VeloxQ at 512–2,048 variables
narration: VeloxQ solves larger QUBOs of the same meal model, from five hundred twelve to two thousand forty-eight variables. We preserve integer packets, verify the spin convention and check raw returned schedules. The initial cold runs return few feasible plans. This establishes the integration and identifies the next experiment: improve feasible solution quality under a fixed budget.

live_narration: VeloxQ solves the larger version of this same meal model: five hundred twelve to two thousand forty-eight variables. We verify the coefficient conversion and every returned schedule. The initial settings expose a feasibility bottleneck; the final comparison will measure usable-plan quality and runtime.

title: Results and implementation
narration: The checked schedule serves twenty meals with no discarded portions. During development, we corrected recovery cleaning and separated portfolio restriction from solver quality. The repository contains the formulation, proofs, raw results and development log.
